verdict.headline: ROST's +10% comps reframes the retail picture as NVDA and Jackson Hole week opens
verdict.label: Off-price beats full-price; Brent $93 holds below $94 trigger; BTC $77.7K on Clarity Act; 30Y contained at 5.24%
verdict.rationale_short: ROST's second consecutive +10% comp quarter — EPS $2.66 vs $1.94, traffic-driven — reframes Thursday's WMT miss as format-specific demand response rather than broad consumer deceleration. Retail gauntlet final: HD, TGT, and ROST all beat; WMT missed. Brent at $93.01 held below the $94 regime trigger; 30Y at 5.24% held below the 5.30% bear threshold. The read changes if Brent closes above $94 before NVDA's Aug 26 print, or if Warsh at Jackson Hole frames oil as a higher-for-longer signal rather than a supply disruption.

trade_setups.asset: ROST — off-price trade-down confirmed at double-digit comps
trade_setups.thesis: ROST's second consecutive +10% comp quarter on record traffic confirms the consumer trade-down thesis. The $0.60/share IEEPA tariff refund (~$253M) is real but non-repeating; traffic-driven comp volume is not a refund artifact. Ex-refund, Q2 EPS would be approximately $2.06 — still above the $1.94 consensus. The WMT/ROST divergence is format-specific: WMT deploys tariff refunds as price cuts to defend traffic; ROST captures incremental spend from consumers trading down in format. Full-year EPS raised to $8.61-$8.77; store openings raised to 115.
trade_setups.entry: AH reference print ~$247. The consolidation level to watch through Friday: $240 is the intraday floor that separates structural re-rating from gap-and-fade. Pullback into $235-240 in the context of broader market pressure would retest the pre-earnings high zone.
trade_setups.invalidation: ROST opens below $235 on broad retail sector de-rating driven by the WMT demand-softening narrative overriding the off-price separation trade. Or: tariff refund one-time nature dominates sell-side consensus revision into the close.
trade_setups.horizon: 4-6 weeks; Q3 October earnings is the next fundamental catalyst.

trade_setups.asset: BTC — Clarity Act regulatory catalyst; $77.7K from $62K Gate 2
trade_setups.thesis: BTC has extended from $62K Gate 2 to $77,656 — a 25%+ move driven by two sequential regulatory events: the SEC's proposed crypto regulation (Aug 19) and Trump's Clarity Act White House push (Aug 20). The move has diverged from equity tape (BTC up 8% overnight while SPX futures fell). ETH at $2,261 (+18% from Tuesday) is confirming. The $80K round number is the next psychological ceiling.
trade_setups.entry: The levels: $70K is the Clarity Act momentum breakthrough point; $62K (Gate 2) remains the structural floor; $80K is the next ceiling to watch. $68K on two consecutive closes is the momentum-exhaustion signal.
trade_setups.invalidation: BTC closes below $68K on two consecutive sessions — signals the regulatory catalyst is fully priced ahead of the legislative process. Below $62K invalidates the breakout.
trade_setups.horizon: 1-3 weeks; Clarity Act Senate legislative timeline is the primary variable.

bear_case: ROST's $0.60/share IEEPA tariff refund (~$253M) is non-repeating; ex-refund, the FY EPS guide of $8.61-$8.77 reverts to approximately $8.01-$8.17. WMT covers 140 million weekly US shoppers and its CFO used direct demand-softening language — off-price trade-down expands in adversity, but if WMT's Q3 EPS guide ($0.62-$0.64 vs $0.73 consensus) proves accurate rather than conservative, the consumer deceleration case is structural, not format-specific. Brent at $93.01 remains $0.99 from the $94 formal trigger; the 30Y is 6 basis points from the 5.30% bear threshold established Thursday. BTC's +7.75% overnight move on a crypto bill with no confirmed Senate floor date is event-driven momentum until a vote schedule materializes. NVDA enters the print 5 trading days out at $216.95 with AMD 17 points below its containment signal. If NVDA's result lands in-line with the elevated bar rather than materially above it — and Warsh at Jackson Hole frames Brent at $93+ as a higher-for-longer supply signal rather than a transitory disruption — the current premarket bid would reverse sharply. The level where the constructive read breaks: Brent closes above $94 AND 30Y closes above 5.30% before NVDA's Aug 26 print.
